item.title: FG suspends broadcast licence fee reviews indefinitely
item.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Federal Government has suspended all reviews of broadcast licence fees indefinitely following concerns by operators over rising operational costs and financial pressures facing Nigeria’s broadcasting industry. The Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, announced the decision on Monday in Abuja during a courtesy visit by a delegation of the Broadcasting Organisations of Nigeria (BON), led by its Chairman, Senior High Chief Dr Tony Akiotu. The decision followed BON’s 82nd General Assembly in Calabar, Cross River State, where the organisation raised concerns about the sustainability of broadcast operations amid mounting economic challenges. In a statement issued on Monday night by the Minister’s Special Assistant on Media, Rabiu Ibrahim, Idris said the suspension was part of efforts by the Federal Government to create a more conducive operating environment for broadcasters. “Any increase in licence fees is hereby put on hold. All reviews relating to licences are suspended until further notice. I am directing the NBC to ensure strict compliance while we review the situation,” he said. The minister also directed the Director-General of the National Broadcasting Commission (NBC) to expedite the review of the National Broadcasting Code to ensure that its provisions reflect current developments and emerging realities in the industry. On the Digital Switch-Over (DSO) programme, Idris promised to convene a stakeholders’ meeting to address outstanding concerns and resolve challenges affecting its implementation. He further disclosed that he had directed the Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria (ARCON) to ensure full enforcement of the 45-day payment period for advertising services, following BON’s request for improved compliance with the policy. The minister also assured the delegation that the ministry would engage relevant stakeholders on concerns surrounding access to affordable financing and spectrum allocation. Describing broadcasting as critical to national development, Idris said the industry played an important role in strengthening democracy, promoting national cohesion and ensuring public access to credible and accurate information. With the 2027 general elections approaching, he urged broadcasters to uphold professionalism, fairness and ethical standards in their reportage. “Freedom of expression must go with responsibility. You cannot simply say anything and claim to be practising journalism. “Journalism has standards, procedures and ethics. I urge broadcasters to ensure that what they report is factual, responsible and promotes national unity and peaceful coexistence,” the minister said. Earlier, BON Chairman, Akiotu, commended Idris for his intervention during the June 2026 DSO launch, noting that the stakeholders’ meeting convened by the minister helped address concerns about ensuring a level playing field for operators. item.title: Turkey Steel Factory Explosion Kills 16, Injures 13
item.description: An explosion ripped through a steel plant in western Turkey on Monday, killing 16 people and injuring 13, President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said, announcing investigations into the tragedy. Eight workers were trapped at the HABAS steel factory about 60 kilometres (37 miles) north of the port city of Izmir, where the blast struck around midday (0900 GMT), said Izmir governor Suleyman Elban. Footage posted online showed a huge cloud of thick smoke pouring into the sky as flames appeared to engulf a tall structure within the HABAS Demir Celik plant in Aliaga. “The circumstances surrounding this tragic incident, which has deeply saddened our nation, including how and why it happened, whether there was any negligence, and who bears responsibility, will be established,” Erdogan said on television. Turkey’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan talks with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung during their meeting at the presidential Blue House in Seoul on November 3, 2026. Photo by JEON HEON-KYUN / POOL / AFP He said two of the injured were in serious condition. HABAS is a privately owned group and one of Turkey’s top steel producers. Crane Collapse According to Izmir’s governor, the blast was caused by an overhead crane that collapsed into a large industrial furnace used during the liquid steel casting process. “While a boiler replacement operation was being carried out at the HABAS iron and steel factory, the overhead crane fell and landed in the arc furnace, causing an explosion in the steel mill behind it,” Elban told reporters, referring to a large electric-powered steelmaking furnace. An eyewitness, Deniz Ulker, said it felt like an “earthquake”. “When I looked at the factory across the street, thick black smoke was coming out. A fire broke out where the chimney was,” Ulker told Anadolu news agency. “It was like a bomb going off,” said Turan Ilbay, who works as a truck driver at the factory and also spoke to Anadolu. Izmir mayor Cemil Tugay said on X that rescue teams were “continuing their work to remove the collapsed platform” and that those affected were factory workers. Safety Issues Workers’ groups said there was a long record of safety issues at HABAS. Contacted by an AFP journalist, HABAS declined to answer questions. Before Monday’s explosion, the Evrensel daily said at least 11 workers had died over the past decade while working there. Turkey’s Labour Party, a small Marxist faction, said on X it was the third time in three weeks that workers had lost their lives at HABAS. It said one man died after falling eight metres (26 feet) from a ladder on October 21, while another died when a tyre he was inflating on a construction machine exploded. Outside the hospital where the injured were taken, two representatives of the leftist Aegean Workers’ Collective were arrested while trying to make a statement about workplace safety issues, a group spokesman said. “The HABAS management’s blind greed for profit has resulted in a major disaster today,” their spokes

item.title: 2027: Why we’re yet to print over 2.9m PVCs — INEC
item.description: ….Removes 1,609,553 multiple, deceased registrants ….Identifies 54 staff responsible for multiple registration, unusual registration patterns, substituted photos ….Yet to receive CTC of judgment on Atiku/ADC By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has explained why those who registered in the third phase of its Continuous Voter Registration CVR are yet to have their Permanent Voter Cards even as it announced a massive purge of the national voter register ahead of the 2027 general elections. Addressing a press conference in Abuja, the INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Ojo Amupitan, SAN, disclosed that the commission has successfully removed 1,609,553 invalid and deceased records from the system. “The Commission recognises that the detection of irregularities raises legitimate questions about how they arose. The response is evidence-led investigation, completed corrective action and stronger preventive controls. “1,609,553 records have been removed, comprising 1,608,660 confirmed invalid registrations and 873 verified deceased-voter records. INEC will continue to communicate verifiable aggregate outcomes while protecting personal information and the integrity of ongoing investigations”, said Amupitan. Addressing reporters regarding the status of unprinted cards, the INEC Chairman stated: “The distribution of Phases 1 and 2 of the PVC and transferred PVCs is on-going at the various LGAs in Nigeria. Some of the PVC for the third and final Phase are being delivered and they would be dispatched to the States by next week. “Meanwhile as from 1st December 2026, distribution will go back to the Registration Areas all over Nigeria. We appeal to those that registered in the third phase to be a little bit patient since the production is done outside the country”. Vanguard recalls that those who registered in total in the third phase were 2,970,257 before the commission’s de-duplication protocol. The sweeping clean-up of the register followed widespread public outcry and intense scrutiny over anomalies spotted on the preliminary register displayed between October 9 and 15, 2026. A rigorous technical audit utilizing the Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) uncovered systemic manipulations, including unusual registration patterns, substituted photographs, and fraudulent multiple registrations. Crucially, the investigation indicted internal personnel who abused their offices. Prof. Amupitan revealed that the commission identified 54 staff members cutting across 10 states who deliberately bypassed standard operating procedures and exploited special provisions meant for vulnerable citizens, such as persons with disabilities. Disciplinary actions and possible prosecutions have been initiated against the culprits. item.title: You can grab three months of Game Pass Ultimate for under $20 per month
item.description: The price of Xbox Game Pass Ultimate has fluctuated between $20 and $30 per month over the last year, but you can get three months of the top plan for around $19 per month. At Newegg , using the coupon code BNWF2656 at checkout knocks $11 off the usual cost of a three-month subscription. That brings the price down to just $57.99 for three months. In addition to full access to over 500 games on both Xbox consoles and Windows PC machines, the upgraded Ultimate plan includes EA Play and Ubisoft Plus Classics, which have their own libraries and benefits, and Fortnite Crew for full access to the Fortnite battles passes. On Xbox, Ultimate enables online multiplayer, as well. Xbox Game Pass Ultimate (three-month subscription) Where to Buy: $68.99 $57.99 at Newegg (w/ promo code BNWF2656) Previously a straightforward proposition, the service has undergone a variety of changes over the last year that has made it slightly less appealing. Xbox Game Pass Ultimate was previously $29.99 per month, but earlier this year Microsoft removed the Call of Duty games from the library, and in the process dropped the price to $22.99. More recently, Microsoft added hourly limits to cloud gaming . All Game Pass plan subscribers previously enjoyed an unlimited amount of cloud gaming on their computer or mobile device, but now plans scale the number of included hours, with the Ultimate plan including 15 hours per month. That news came just weeks before announcing pay-as-you-go plans for non-Game Pass subscribers. Other deals to consider The AMD Ryzen 7 9700X is discounted to $269 at various retailers, including Amazon , Best Buy , and B&H , a $70 break from the usual price. This eight-core, 16-thread desktop CPU is compatible with AM5 motherboards, and has a maximum boost clock of up to 5.5GHz out of the box, with full support for overclocking. It’s probably overkill for light gaming, but serious gamers and demanding PC users will get the a lot of bang for their buck with this AMD processor. The discounted price lets you reach near AMD’s fastest consumer chip offerings, and is much cheaper than the faster Ryzen 7 9800X3D . This Lego Pokémon Pikachu and Pokéball set is on sale for $159.95 at Amazon . That $40 discount is the largest we’ve seen since the collaboration launched back in March , and a remarkably good value for a set with 2,050 pieces. Once built, it’s a sizable set, standing 13.5 inches tall and 15.5 inches deep, and the Pikachu has posable ears and limbs. This seems like a fantastic gift, either to yourself or to another Pokémon fan you care about. Amazon has the Bose Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar marked down to $899, a $200 discount from the usual price. This Dolby Atmos-equipped soundbar supports eARC over HDMI, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth connectivity for easy adjustments or listening to music, and has Alexa voice commands for when you can’t find the remote. You can also combine the soundbar with Bose Lifestyle Ultra Speakers for a proper surround system.

item.title: TenTrade brings financial market experts together to promote trading education in Lagos
item.description: Financial services company, TenTrade, has brought together financial market experts, traders and industry stakeholders in Lagos to discuss ways of expanding participation in financial markets and preparing the next generation of traders. The gathering, held in Ikeja on Saturday, November 7, 2026, was themed, “One Community, One Future: Building the Next Generation of Traders.” The event featured discussions on financial market education, trading opportunities and the future of the trading industry in Africa. Speaking at the event, Wilfred Obasi, Regional Director for Africa at TenTrade, identified impatience and the desire to make quick money as major challenges confronting young traders. “For young traders, they are not patient enough. People want to make quick money. It is why we are making the event work today to enlighten young traders,” Obasi said. He explained that the event was organised to expose young people to the realities of financial trading and help them develop the patience and knowledge required to navigate the market. Obasi also spoke about the company’s international expansion, noting that TenTrade had grown from operating in one or two regions to having a presence in about 30 countries, including Kenya, Ghana, Nigeria and Indonesia. He attributed the company’s growth to its emphasis on building trust and empowering clients. “We make sure that we do not overpromise. We empower our clients and we do well for them,” he said. Also speaking, Ademola Adeagbo, Head of Education at TenTrade Africa, urged traders to prioritise risk management, discipline and trading psychology to achieve consistency in the financial markets. He identified fear, greed, fear of missing out (FOMO) and revenge trading as common emotional traps that could undermine trading decisions and expose traders to losses. Adeagbo stressed that traders must develop the discipline to manage risks and avoid making decisions based on emotions. Similarly, Kehinde Shogeke, TenTrade’s Sales Team Lead, said traders needed adequate market knowledge, sufficient capital and discipline to improve their chances of navigating the financial markets. He observed that many people entered forex trading without understanding its fundamentals, viewing it instead as an opportunity to make quick money. “Most traders or new traders see forex as a get-rich-quickly scheme. There is a basic knowledge of the market that they must have. Have a good knowledge, capital and discipline,” he said. Shogeke further explained that TenTrade offered different account options to accommodate traders with varying needs, including regular brokerage and funded accounts. According to him, the company’s regular brokerage offering provides up to six types of accounts, while its equity account allows traders to access up to $500,000. He described the combination of brokerage and funded trading accounts as one of the company’s distinctive offerings. Meanwhile, a TenTrade partner, Peace Ohikhena, said her relationsh

item.title: Nasarawa APC protests alleged violence, SDP alleges bias
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia Members and supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Nasarawa State on Monday staged a protest in Lafia over alleged political violence, intimidation of party members and the disruption of the party’s presidential rally attended by Vice President Kashim Shettima. Addressing journalists and security officials during the demonstration, the state APC Chairman, Dr. Aliyu Bello, called for investigations into reported attacks on party supporters, including the alleged killing of a supporter in the Tudun Wada area of Lafia. Bello expressed concern over what he described as the failure of law enforcement agencies to act on complaints previously submitted by the party. He said the protest was organised to demand justice and adequate protection for party members, insisting that the APC remained committed to peaceful political activities. “We came here to demand justice that a full-scale investigation be carried out and the perpetrators of these acts arrested and prosecuted,” he said. The APC chairman also raised concerns about alleged threats and conduct by some opposition figures, calling on security agencies to ensure that all political actors operate within the law. Responding on behalf of Governor Abdullahi Sule, the Deputy Governor, Dr Emmanuel Akabe, described the reported incidents as a matter of concern and criticised the security arrangements surrounding the disruption of the Vice-President’s rally. Akabe said security agencies had been briefed ahead of Shettima’s visit and stressed that protecting lives and property remained their responsibility. “It is unfortunate because the responsibility of security men is to protect lives and property. If you cannot protect individuals in your state, then a lot needs to be answered,” he said. The deputy governor disclosed that the State Emergency Security Council had convened to consider measures to prevent further disturbances. He assured the protesters that the state government would support efforts to ensure that anyone found culpable was dealt with in accordance with the law. Speaking on behalf of the Nasarawa State Police Command, Assistant Commissioner of Police Gaya Ahmed reaffirmed the neutrality of security agencies and their commitment to investigating complaints. “The IGP has made it clear that the police are neutral, and we keep on maintaining that neutrality,” Ahmed said. He assured the protesters that petitions submitted by the APC would be forwarded to the incoming Commissioner of Police for investigation. A representative of the Department of State Services (DSS), the Deputy Director of Administration, also acknowledged receipt of the party’s complaints and commended the protesters for conducting themselves peacefully without obstructing public roads. However, the Nasarawa State chapter of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) criticised the demonstration, accusing the state government and the APC of using the protest to target opposition figures. item.title: Court dismisses Maihaja’s suit against Wali’s APC ticket
item.description: By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman, Damaturu A Federal High Court sitting in Damaturu, Yobe State, has dismissed a suit challenging the emergence of Alhaji Baba Malam Wali as the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for the 2027 general election. The suit was instituted by Engr. Mustapha Yunusa Maihaja, an aspirant in the party’s May 21 governorship primary, who alleged irregularities and non-compliance with the APC’s electoral guidelines. In a judgment delivered on Monday, November 9, 2026, Justice Fatima Murtala Amin held that the suit was statute-barred, having been filed outside the legally prescribed timeframe. The court also found that Maihaja failed to establish his allegations, particularly the claim of over-voting during the governorship primary. Justice Amin upheld a preliminary objection challenging the competence of the suit, thereby dismissing the case on procedural grounds. On the substantive issues, the judge identified material contradictions and inconsistencies in the testimonies of the plaintiff’s witnesses, describing the evidence as unreliable and insufficient to support the allegations. The court further held that even if the suit had been filed within the prescribed timeframe, it would still have failed on its merits because the plaintiff did not provide credible evidence to establish the alleged over-voting. Wali emerged winner of the APC governorship primary with 236,711 votes, securing the party’s ticket for the 2027 governorship election in the state. Reacting to the judgment, Wali’s Press Secretary, Shuaibu Abdullahi, commended the court for its consideration of the issues raised in the suit. “We commend the Court for its painstaking consideration of the issues and reaffirm our confidence in the judiciary as the ultimate guardian of justice and the rule of law,” Abdullahi said. The judgment dismisses the legal challenge to Wali’s emergence as the APC governorship candidate, leaving his party ticket intact ahead of the 2027 general election. The post Court dismisses Maihaja’s suit against Wali’s APC ticket appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Offa robbery: Saraki faults Kwara govt over amended charges
item.description: Former Senate President, Bukola Saraki, has criticised the Kwara State Government over its decision to amend the criminal charges filed against him and former Governor Abdulfatah Ahmed in connection with the 2018 Offa bank robbery. Saraki described the development as an abuse of the judicial process, questioning the basis for the government’s decision to drop 18 of the original 20 counts and proceed with an amended four-count charge. In a statement issued on Monday by his media aide, Yusuph Olaniyonu, the former Senate President accused the administration of Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq of pursuing the case for political reasons. The Kwara State Government had, in an application filed on Monday before the state High Court in Ilorin, sought permission to proceed with an amended four-count charge against Saraki, Ahmed and two other defendants. The amended charge, dated November 6, 2026, retains two allegations bordering on conspiracy to belong to a gang of thieves and belonging to a gang of thieves. It also introduces two additional counts relating to the alleged concealment of a Lexus RX Jeep bearing the inscription ‘SARAKI’ as its plate number. Reacting, Saraki said the government had abandoned 18 charges relating to armed robbery after allegedly failing to establish a case against him and Ahmed. He said the government had, since April 2026, been pursuing their arraignment at the State High Court and the Court of Appeal without success. “Last weekend, the state government that has set its legal team to be shuttling between the State High Court and the Court of Appeal seeking without success since April 2026 to arraign the two predecessors of Mr Abdulrazaq on charges of armed robbery suddenly made a U-turn and dropped all 18 charges relating to armed robbery on the Offa case,” the statement said. Saraki alleged that the decision to amend the charges followed the government’s inability to substantiate the allegations against the two former governors. “For fear of failure, the government has chosen to change gear and explore yet other baseless charges,” he said. He described the amendment as evidence, in his view, that the allegations against him and Ahmed lacked a credible factual foundation. “The amendment to the charge sheet only reveals that there was no case against these gentlemen from the beginning and what the state government is indulging in is abuse of powers, a travesty of the justice system, and mockery of the prosecutorial powers of the state,” he added. The former Senate President also questioned the government’s decision to discontinue the 18 counts after allegedly spending close to N100 million publicising its claims against the defendants in national newspapers earlier in the year. He argued that the money could have been channelled into public projects rather than prosecuting allegations he described as unfounded. item.title: Barcelona teenager Pau Cubarsí wins 2026 Golden Boy Award
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Barcelona centre-back Pau Cubarsí has won the 2026 Golden Boy award, becoming the first defender since Matthijs de Ligt in 2018 to receive the honour. The 19-year-old was recognised after a standout year with Barcelona and Spain. He helped Barça win a second consecutive LaLiga title and was part of Spain’s World Cup-winning team in North America, where he was named Young Player of the Tournament. “I’m very proud to receive the award, and I thank all the people who voted for me,” Cubarsí said in a video broadcast by Tuttosport at the ceremony. “It’s been a spectacular year, and we’re going for more,” he added. Cubarsí told Reuters that defenders can struggle to attract the same attention as attacking players. “It’s harder for defenders to get recognition… we’re less in the spotlight,” he said. “Perhaps our work isn’t as visible because, at the end of the day, the forwards score lots of goals, provide assists, play a more attractive style of football, are more eye-catching.” Spain conceded only one goal in eight matches en route to winning the World Cup, and Cubarsí played a key role in the team’s defence. He becomes the fourth Barcelona player to win the men’s award in the last six years, following teammates Pedri, Gavi and Lamine Yamal. Previous winners include Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappé and Erling Haaland. The Golden Boy award, established by Italian newspaper Tuttosport in 2003, recognises the best under-21 player in a top European division. Journalists vote from a shortlist of nominees. Real Madrid and Sweden forward Felicia Schroeder won the 2026 Golden Girl award. The post Barcelona teenager Pau Cubarsí wins 2026 Golden Boy Award appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu: Wike promises N10m reward for FCT Councillors who deliver for APC
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has announced a financial incentive of N10 million for every councillor who successfully delivers their respective political ward for the All Progressives Congress APC and President Bola Tinubu in the upcoming general elections. Addressing stakeholders, traditional leaders, and political actors in Kwali, Wike explained that the initiative is part of a broad grassroots mobilisation strategy designed to rally maximum support at the grassroots level. “Any councillor that delivers his ward will get N10 million reward. Therefore, go and meet your leaders, go and meet your youth groups, go and consult with associations. Let’s deliver our ward to Mr President,” Wike urged the gathering. In addition to the electoral incentive, the FCT minister addressed structural and welfare concerns raised by local leaders, notably responding to an appeal by the Chairman of the National Councillors Forum of Nigeria (FCT Chapter), Gambo Hamza. Hamza had drawn attention to the disparity and low earnings of councillors in the territory – noting a monthly salary of N260,000 – which Wike termed unacceptable. The Minister promised to engage the permanent secretary and relevant administrative offices to review the remuneration structure, bypassing bureaucratic bottlenecks where possible to improve local governance welfare. Wike also underscored his administration’s dedication to gender inclusivity, emphasizing the need to increase women’s active participation in governance. Wike did not also mince words regarding what he described as the historical marginalisation of the FCT. He pointed out the stark disproportion in legislative distribution, questioning how a fast-growing population of six to seven million residents is restricted to only one Senate seat and a minimal number of House of Representatives seats. Comparing the FCT to other states with lesser populations boasting three senators and up to ten representatives, Wike maintained that structural fairness must be championed to give the nation’s capital adequate voice and equity. The post Tinubu: Wike promises N10m reward for FCT Councillors who deliver for APC appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Russell Brand jailed for 10 years for rape, assault
item.description: British comedian and TV star Russell Brand was Monday jailed for more than 10 years for a string of sex offences including rape, as the judge told him he had been a “sexual predator” whose fame had protected him. Brand, 51, showed no emotion as judge Joel Bennathan said he had acted with “staggering arrogance” and shown “contempt” for his victims, who had suffered significant and lasting harm. “About 20 years ago Russell Brand, you were becoming famous, you were clever, and in many people’s eyes you were funny and charismatic. You had also become a sexual predator,” he said. The judge said Brand’s status protected him until he was exposed in 2023 by journalists from the Sunday Times, The Times and the Channel 4 Dispatches programme, leading to women coming forward to make complaints to police. Bennathan paid tribute to the “determination and bravery” of the women, adding Brand had repeatedly acted “how you liked and when you liked, unhindered by the rules by which decent people live”. Brand’s wife Laura Gallacher, with whom he has three children, slumped in her seat in the public gallery of London’s Southwark Crown Court as the total sentence of 10 years and six months was announced. Brand told his wife, who has supported him in court throughout the case, “we’ll be OK”, before being led down to the cells. The disgraced star was convicted by a jury last week of one rape and three sexual assaults committed against four women between 2004 and 2009. Brand, who has reinvented himself as an online Christian guru, held a string of prayer beads and made the sign of the cross before one of his victims personally read out her impact statement from behind a screen. She said she had been left “traumatised” by the assault in a London bar in 2004. “For many years as his star was rising it was impossible to escape seeing him all over the media, being celebrated for his disgusting behaviour against women like it was all a joke,” she told the court. ‘Celebrated’ A second woman, a 21-year-old fan he raped in 2009 after they met at one of his shows, told the court she had felt she simply would “not be believed” if she reported him. “His fame, wealth and influence created a power imbalance which made me feel powerless,” she said. The hearing came as Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged to be “relentless in making whatever improvements we can” to provide more support for victims. Brand was cleared of two other alleged rapes and one count of attempted indecent assault. But he is facing further investigations after London police revealed rape allegations by two more women. From Channel 4 to MTV and an eponymous primetime show on BBC Radio 2, the wild-haired comedian’s obsession with sex and his no-holds barred delivery contributed to his notoriety. item.title: Starfish Space loses contact with 1st 'Otter' servicing spacecraft, ending NASA tech-demo mission
item.description: null Starfish Space's first Otter has died, just a month after it reached the final frontier. The Seattle startup announced on Tuesday (Nov. 3) that its Otter 24C satellite suffered a glitch in low Earth orbit (LEO) and is not recoverable. The anomaly killed an ambitious mission in the cradle, as Otter 24C was still in the commissioning phase. Otter 24C launched Oct. 1 on SpaceX 's Transporter-18 mission, a rideshare flight that carried a total of 130 payloads to LEO (including a prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher , Google's planned AI constellation). The Starfish satellite was flying a mission for NASA called Small Spacecraft Propulsion and Inspection Capability, or SSPICY for short. The goal was to "demonstrate technologies necessary for future debris-removal missions as well as for future applications in the servicing and inspection of active spacecraft," according to NASA's SSPICY site . "This advances NASA's in-space manufacturing and assembly (ISAM) goals to ensure a sustainable space operating environment and builds towards a future where objects can be assembled, repaired and maintained in space, significantly expanding possibilities for science and human exploration," the agency added. Starfish Space was a natural partner. The Seattle company plans to become a big player in the nascent field of satellite servicing , using its line of Otter craft to repair, refuel or deorbit other satellites for a variety of customers. Illustration of a Starfish Space Otter satellite rendesvousing with another spacecraft in Earth orbit. (Image credit: Starfish Space) SSPICY marked Otter's spaceflight debut. The mission plan called for the 739-pound (335-kilogram) Otter 24C spacecraft to approach and inspect "up to four inoperable space objects of U.S. origin" over the course of a two-year mission, performing detailed visual inspections. But Otter 24C never got the chance to perform any of these orbital rendezvous. "While working through commissioning steps, Starfish eventually stopped receiving data from Otter 24C," the company said in a Nov. 3 X post . "An investigation into the loss of communications has determined that fault protection on the satellite bus provided by [California company] Astro Digital had an error that turned off the radio and prevented re-establishing communications," Starfish added. "Starfish, NASA, and Astro Digital have concluded that Otter 24C is not recoverable." The company further said that it's implementing fixes to reduce the chances that the problem will crop up in the future. And it stressed that Otter 24C's death will not be in vain. "The work completed through Otter 24C will directly contribute to the success of future Otter missions, as Starfish continues developing the technologies and operations required to make satellite servicing a routine capability in orbit," Starfish said. item.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
item.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. However, for raw materials such as cowhide, I usually source these from local abattoirs while sisal and tree barks are either harvested by me or sometimes extracted by colleagues I work with, who are based in the rural areas.” Desmond Ntini , a cultural entrepreneur based in Bulawayo, sees Malunga’s work as part of a broader shift in how African history is perceived and used. ” Malunga is redefining the fashion industry by blending traditional African influences with contemporary creativity. Her work explains how our cultural identity can inspire modern designs while opening doors for sustainable fashion, business opportunities, and the celebration of African heritage.” Ntini said. item.title: 2027: Stop following Tinubu to rallies, return to grassroots, Kalu tells APC leaders
item.description: Senator Orji Uzor Kalu has urged leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to stop following President Bola Tinubu from one campaign rally to another and concentrate on grassroots mobilisation in their respective states, local government areas and wards ahead of the 2027 general elections. Kalu, who represents Abia North Senatorial District and serves as Coordinator of Parliamentary Mobilisation for the South-East, made the call in a statement titled, “The APC Presidential Campaign Council and the Need for a Leaner Campaign Train.” He argued that Tinubu should be accompanied by a smaller campaign team, while other party leaders should remain in their respective political bases to engage voters and strengthen the party’s grassroots structures. The senator’s position comes days after the APC Presidential Campaign Council issued guidelines restricting ministers, political appointees and campaign council members to rallies organised in their respective home states. The circular, signed by the Director-General of the council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, on November 3, was addressed to directors and heads of directorates. It directed political appointees and other campaign officials to attend only rallies in their home states as part of efforts to improve coordination and grassroots mobilisation. The council also adopted what it described as the pyramid concept of mobilisation, which prioritises engagement at polling unit, ward, local government and state levels. Under the arrangement, campaign officials and party leaders are expected to concentrate on building support at the grassroots rather than concentrating around the President during rallies. Kalu cited his political activities in Abia State as an example of the importance of grassroots mobilisation. He recalled leading more than 4,000 APC members in his Igbere Ward A, Bende Local Government Area, during the party’s presidential primary in May. He said the exercise demonstrated the importance of building political support from the ward level. At the exercise, the returning officer, Mr Ulu Onwuchekwa, announced that Tinubu scored 4,986 votes in the ward. Tinubu had also urged members of the campaign council to take responsibility for mobilisation across the country, saying he would concentrate on governance. The President made the appeal on October 14 during the inauguration of the Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja. The campaign was subsequently flagged off in Kaduna on October 24, with plans to take the campaign to all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. Tinubu is, however, expected to personally attend rallies in only 12 states. The November 3 circular further directed campaign directorates without specific responsibilities at rallies to concentrate on their approved work plans and budgets. item.title: NASA Advanced Mid-Power Electric Rocket Challenge
item.description: 1 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) This Hall-effect thruster, shown being tested at Glenn Research Center, turns electricity and inert gas into force that could propel a spacecraft. Orbion Space Technology was founded to bring the high efficiency of these thrusters to small commercial satellites, and the company sought the center’s help to make that a reality. Credit: NASA Mid-power (3-7 kW) Hall effect thruster systems have been identified by government and industry stakeholders as critical capabilities for satellite, defense, and exploration missions. Given the need for this capability, NASA is launching the Advanced Mid-Power Electric Rocket (AMPERE) Challenge. The NASA AMPERE Challenge invites U.S. commercial companies to develop and demonstrate mid-power Hall effect thruster prototypes. Through this challenge, NASA aims to accelerate the maturation of electric propulsion capabilities, validate real-world performance in NASA test facilities, and build the foundation needed to support future NASA and commercial missions. The challenge is open to companies incorporated in and maintaining a primary place of business in the United States. Award: $500,000 in total prizes. Up to two winning teams can each receive up to $250,000 in cash prizes, plus access to NASA testing and technology, across three phases. Registration Open Date: November 9, 2026 Registration Close Date: January 27, 2027 For more information including registration , rules, and eligibility, visit: https://ampere.nasatechmaturation.org/

item.title: La NASA destina un millón de dólares al reto estudiantil Base Lunar
item.description: Representación artística en la que se muestran astronautas, hábitats, rovers, sistemas de energía y operaciones de carga que permiten mantener actividades humanas continuadas en la Base Lunar, situada cerca del Polo Sur lunar. Crédito: NASA Read this release in English here . El domingo 8 de noviembre de 2026, la NASA anunció la convocatoria del reto estudiantil Base Lunar, dotado con un millón de dólares, durante un acto de MAX POWER celebrado en el Complejo de Visitantes del Centro Espacial Kennedy, en Florida. En el marco de una edad de oro de la ciencia, la competición invita a equipos de estudiantes de escuelas secundarias y centros de educación superior de Estados Unidos a aportar diseños para la Base Lunar. “Buscamos estudiantes dispuestos a pensar de forma creativa, a trabajar en equipo y a abordar problemas reales relacionados con el futuro de la NASA en la Luna”, dijo el administrador de la NASA, Jared Isaacman. “No hace falta esperar hasta la graduación para contribuir. La curiosidad, la creatividad y la voluntad de afrontar problemas difíciles sin respuestas obvias son precisamente las cualidades que necesitamos mientras construimos lo que viene a continuación”. La NASA está construyendo la Base Lunar, donde los astronautas vivirán, trabajarán y explorarán la región del Polo Sur lunar. La presencia humana permanente en la Luna allana el camino para futuras misiones tripuladas a Marte y requiere talento procedente de diversos sectores y ámbitos. “A medida que construimos y diseñamos los cimientos de la Base Lunar, queremos aprovechar todo el ingenio y la innovación para tener en cuenta cada aspecto que nuestros exploradores puedan necesitar para vivir y trabajar allí”, afirmó Carlos García-Galán, director del programa Base Lunar. “Los estudiantes aportan precisamente las ideas audaces que estamos buscando, y estoy deseando descubir su enfoque. En definitiva, la Base Lunar es para ellos, las personas que vivirán en un mundo en el que los seres humanos estarán en la Luna para quedarse”. Este reto, que consta de varias fases, refuerza el compromiso de la NASA con el desarrollo de las competencias técnicas del personal aeroespacial del futuro. Los equipos de estudiantes diseñarán soluciones innovadoras para la Base Lunar en seis categorías: generación y almacenamiento de energía, construcción, sistemas de soporte vital, movilidad en la superficie, redes de comunicaciones y seguridad de los astronautas. La iniciativa ofrece a los participantes la oportunidad de adquirir las aptitudes necesarias para una carrera en la industria espacial, al tiempo que contribuye al avance de nuevos conceptos tecnológicos para la Base Lunar. Los participantes deben inscribirse en el reto a través de la plataforma NASA STEM Gateway , en inglés. El plazo de inscripción está abierto hasta el 25 de enero de 2027. “Los estudiantes son la siguiente generación de exploradores e innovadores. item.title: Man Utd delay decision on Carrick’s future after dropping into relegation zone — report
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United are not in a hurry to sack head coach Michael Carrick despite their drop into the Premier League relegation zone following Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, according to Sky Sports . Sky Sports News reports that the club’s hierarchy plan to use the international break to assess the team’s poor start to the season and reconsider their options before making a decision on Carrick’s future. The former United midfielder is under increasing pressure after the club recorded just one win in 11 matches, conceded 30 goals in all competitions and endured what has been described as their worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign. United’s 4-4 draw against Villa followed another comeback in their previous match, but the recent results have not been enough to ease concerns over their overall performances. Carrick and his players were given Monday off after the Villa encounter, with the head coach and his staff expected to return to the club’s Carrington training base on Tuesday. With several players away on international duty and no first-team training sessions scheduled in the coming days, the break is expected to give the club’s leadership time to conduct a broader review. According to Sky Sports, three major factors have contributed to the hierarchy’s decision not to rush a change in the dugout. First, United supporters have not called for Carrick to be dismissed, with the former midfielder still enjoying considerable affection from the fanbase because of his achievements as a player. Carrick won 11 major trophies during his playing career at Old Trafford, including the Champions League and five Premier League titles. Secondly, the club’s hierarchy believe the 45-year-old still has the support of the dressing room, despite the team’s poor form. The recent comebacks against Roma in the Champions League and Aston Villa in the Premier League are understood to have reinforced the belief that the players have not given up on their manager. Thirdly, United’s decision-makers are reportedly not convinced that replacing Carrick would automatically resolve the team’s problems, with the performances of the players also under scrutiny. The report adds that the club could consider available managerial options, including Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe, if they eventually decide to make a change. For now, however, United are expected to take their time before deciding whether Carrick remains the right man to lead the club out of their current crisis. item.description: Former US president Joe Biden says he is scaling back plans to promote his upcoming memoir as he battles aggressive prostate cancer, acknowledging that the illness sometimes leaves him struggling. The 83-year-old Democrat, whose health was a major issue during his presidency, said Sunday that he would be unable to make as many public appearances as he had hoped ahead of the November 17 release of “Promise Me, America.” “Some days are better than others. It hasn’t stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down,” Biden wrote on X. “What that means is, unfortunately, I won’t be able to do as many conversations about my book as I’d hoped. However, I’m hopeful the words on the page speak for themselves.” Biden announced in May 2025, four months after leaving the White House, that he had been diagnosed with an aggressive form of prostate cancer that had spread to his bones. He has since undergone radiation and hormone therapy, while his son Hunter said in August that the disease had spread further and was causing considerable pain. Biden struck an optimistic note about his treatment, saying his doctors “continue to be encouraged” by his response. His memoir chronicles his four years in the White House, including his handling of the Covid-19 pandemic, wars in Afghanistan and Ukraine, and his controversial decision to seek reelection in 2024 before withdrawing. In an excerpt published Monday by The Atlantic, Biden delivered a blistering attack on his successor Donald Trump over the 2021 assault on the US Capitol by supporters seeking to overturn Trump’s election defeat. “What Trump did on January 6, 2021, should never be forgotten. It should follow him to his grave,” Biden wrote. He also recalled an unexpectedly friendly Oval Office meeting with Trump following the Republican’s 2024 election victory, during which his successor suggested they might have been friends outside politics. Biden abandoned his reelection campaign in July 2024 after a disastrous debate against Trump intensified concerns about his age and fitness for office. His vice president, Kamala Harris, subsequently lost the election, returning Trump to the White House. Biden said his book would explain the decisions he made in office and reflect his faith in American democracy. The post Joe Biden scales back book tour as cancer ‘slows me down’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: North Korea Is Minting Its Own Meme Coins to Launder Binance Hack Loot
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine North Korea Is Minting Its Own Meme Coins to Launder Binance Hack Loot North Korean launderers are creating their own worthless meme coins and pushing stolen Binance funds through them so the coins never move directly from one wallet to another, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic said Monday. Between Nov. 5 and 7, the operators minted at least six new tokens on the NEAR blockchain — named FUK, OLCCL, MEILI, MMLI, DABI and SINU — paired each with NEAR in its own liquidity pool, then bought the tokens with stolen NEAR and sold them back out through a second set of wallets. About 117,000 NEAR, or roughly $430,000, passed through the six tokens, Elliptic wrote . The trail sits inside the broader laundering of the Oct. 29 Binance theft, which the exchange has put at $6.34 billion and which the FBI has attributed to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Elliptic’s wider update now puts roughly 3,000 BTC — about $225 million — in new bitcoin addresses converted from other stolen assets, while about 11.8 million NEAR, or $43.7 million, from the theft has still not moved. “Most people think of meme tokens as joke coins whose prices rise and fall on hype,” Elliptic co-founder and chief scientist Dr. Tom Robinson wrote. “North Korea’s launderers have found a different use for them.” How the homemade token trick works The technique is a four-step hop. The North Korea launderers create a token with a public launch tool, open a liquidity pool pairing it with a real asset such as NEAR or a stablecoin, buy the new token with stolen funds from one set of wallets, then sell it back into the same pool from a second set of wallets that collect the real asset. At no point do the stolen funds transfer directly from a buying wallet to a collecting wallet, because the pool sits in between. To a casual observer, the collecting wallets look like ordinary traders who sold a token at a profit. Each of the six NEAR tokens cost about 25 NEAR, or around $90, to create. Each was traded heavily within hours using stolen NEAR and then abandoned. None has traded since Nov. 8, and that afternoon the creators of four of them withdrew what liquidity was left. Five of the six token creators were funded by a wallet that had just sold an earlier token, between two and 13 minutes before the next launch, so the tokens form a chain. Elliptic first reported the same approach in the laundering of the February 2025 Bybit theft, also attributed to North Korean group TraderTraitor, when a worthless Tron token helped move at least $24 million. In the Binance case the firm has also seen the technique on Tron and a close variant on Solana that used existing thinly traded tokens rather than homemade ones. A slowing tactic, not a disappearing act The meme coins do not hide the funds. Every step is public on-chain. What they buy is time. item.title: Claude Code is accidentally exposing secrets all over GitHub
item.description: Claude Code is leaking sensitive information on public GitHub instances thanks to a partial oversight in the way its settings files are handled. That's the finding of AI security researchers at Apiiro, who discovered thousands of secrets , including database passwords, API tokens, and root logins, amid Claude Code settings files embedded in GitHub repositories. The leak stems from the way Claude Code handles user approval for automated shell commands. When a user chooses the "Yes, and don't ask again" option to approve running a command, that choice gets stored as part of a rule in the local ".claude/settings.local.json" file on the user's computer. That rule is sometimes coded as a pattern, but the command itself is often written to that settings file as is, including any sensitive information that may be embedded within it. This isn't really a significant security issue if the settings file stays on the user's local machine (assuming that machine doesn't become compromised itself, of course). And Anthropic notes in its Claude Code documentation that this particular settings file gets added to the developer's global .gitignore list , which usually prevents it from being shared publicly. item.title: TD Cowen Gives Stablecoin Yield Ban 10% Odds as Banks Plan Push in Democrat-Led Congress
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine TD Cowen Gives Stablecoin Yield Ban 10% Odds as Banks Plan Push in Democrat-Led Congress Banks will try again to stop crypto platforms from paying yield on stablecoin balances, but TD Cowen’s Washington analyst Jaret Seiberg puts only a 10% chance on Congress enacting such a ban over the next two years, he wrote in a Monday policy note shared with Bitcoin Magazine and clients. The issue is whether exchanges and other platforms can offer yield or rewards to investors who keep dollar-pegged stablecoins on their platforms. Seiberg views action as unlikely, though he sees a “narrow path” for a ban. His rationale is procedural as much as political: it may be easier to find 60 Senate votes on stablecoin yield alone than on the broader crypto market structure bill, which failed a cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15 and which he already called effectively dead for this Congress after the Democratic midterm sweep. A ban, he wrote, would benefit banks. He expects them to renew the push in the next Congress on the theory that Democratic wins open a path. Why Seiberg still sees a path That path rests on a shift in the Senate. Key crypto advocates retired or lost, while skeptics are being elevated. Sen. Elizabeth Warren is likely to chair the Banking Committee, and Sen. Sherrod Brown, a longtime critic of the industry, regained his Ohio seat after crypto-backed spending of about $64 million failed to stop him, Seiberg wrote before the votes were counted. It is not his base case. Crypto politics are “complex,” he wrote, which is why the probability starts at 10%. Some Democrats will resist treating stablecoin yield outside a broader package. Seiberg again sees no path for the Clarity Act, arguing Democrats will insist on ethics and investor-protection provisions President Trump would reject. That split, he wrote, makes Democrats unlikely to unite behind a yield-only bill. Democrats are not united on the substance either. Sen. Angela Alsobrooks, a lead Democrat on crypto policy, has backed paying rewards for using stablecoins rather than for passively holding them, a distinction that shaped the Tillis-Alsobrooks compromise text during Clarity talks. There is also a perception problem. Congress would be asked to stop voters from earning a return on stablecoin holdings even though they can earn one on savings accounts and money market funds. Seiberg questions whether Democratic leaders want a vote that could be framed as taking money from retail investors. What GENIUS already banned, and what it left open The fight is leftover business from the GENIUS Act, which President Trump signed on July 18, 2025, as Public Law 119-27. The statute bars permitted and foreign payment stablecoin issuers from paying “any form of interest or yield” solely for holding, using or retaining a payment stablecoin. It does not explicitly cover exchanges and other intermediaries. That gap is what banks call the loophole. The American Bankers Association and state bankers asso

item.description: The chipmaker faces business risks and political scrutiny due to its over-reliance on founder and CEO Jensen Huang Why is Nvidia’s Jensen Huang at the centre of a US-China row? One doesn’t have to be overly cynical to think Jensen Huang, the Nvidia boss, starts with one huge advantage as the chipmaker’s board starts its independent investigation into the alleged honeytrap spy scandal . The world of US big tech is not, to put it mildly, strong on checks and balances on a founder’s power. item.title: NASA just launched a $1 million Moon Base Student Challenge to award cash prizes to students that solve lunar base problems
item.description: null CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — NASA has officially launched the Moon Base Student Challenge, asking students to help build humanity's future on the moon. And there's $1 million in prizes up for grabs for the winners. To build and sustain a base on the moon , NASA will have to solve a myriad of problems. And they're looking to the next generation for help, the space agency's chief Jared Isaacman said Sunday (Nov. 8). "We are inviting students from across the country to help solve some of the problems that stand between humanity and a permanent presence on another world," Isaacman said. "We're putting 1 million in prizes together to support the best ideas and recognize the teams behind them." Isaacman made this announcement wearing his blue flight suit from the rocket garden at NASA's Kennedy Space Center Visitor Center amidst the agency's MAX POWER air show event . Just the day before, he flew fighter jets in that suit and even jumped out of a plane, skydiving into the event. Soon after this announcement, he was flying another fighter plane above the crowd. The audience for this announcement was filled with students of all ages. Some young children wearing costume spacesuits squeezed as close as they could to the front of the room while teenagers considering their futures listened intently. It was clear that Isaacman's presence and words were landing with this group. But what moon base challenges does NASA want to see these students tackle? In short, all of them. "The moon base will allow us to conduct groundbreaking science, test new technologies, and prepare again for where we inevitably go next, which is the red planet," he said. "But before any of that can happen, we have an awful lot of problems that need to be solved." "We need ways to generate power through the long lunar night . We need to protect our astronauts from that incredibly harsh and dangerous and demanding environment on the surface. We need to move people and equipment around on the surface and support human life three days away from Earth," Isaacman said, illustrating just a few of the big issues that present with the concept of a moon base. NASA Adminisrator Jared Isaacman invites students to help NASA build a moon base at NASA's Kennedy Space Center Visitor Center. (Image credit: Chelsea Gohd) How will it work? This challenge is open to high school and post-secondary students based in the U.S. For participating students, they will form teams that will work on an idea from one of six different technical topics related to creating and running a moon base. These six topics include power systems, habitats, communications, mobility, life support and astronaut safety . This will be what Isaacman described as a "multi-phase competition that mirrors how ideas are developed actually in the aerospace industry." "Teams will first submit concepts, then they're going to refine them, and finalists will have the opportunity to present their solutions directly to NASA leaders and stakeholders,"

item.title: Machine learning researchers build a better world model
item.description: Machine learning researchers have developed a technique that allows world models to make better predictions about how objects will behave. World models are used to train physical AI systems like robots how to navigate the real world. They predict the consequences of actions. But they do so based on observed data. These models could provide better direction to robots if they were able to make inferences about possible actions without being trained for all the possible outcomes. Randall Balestriero (Brown University, AMI Labs), Kerda Varaku, and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun (NYU, AMI Labs) describe an approach that might allow that to happen in a pre-print paper, "Counterfactual World Models: Natura Non Facit Saltus." The Latin refers to Gottfried Leibniz's axiom " nature makes no leaps ," which had a good run until it ran headlong into quantum mechanics. Yet for the authors, the saying explains how they have been able to devise a method for zero-shot physics inference. Counterfactual world models, said Balestriero in an email to The Register use "the mismatch between your prediction and the real world to figure out what did you get wrong, and from that you can better understand what happened for better future predictions, debugging, reasoning, all at test time." Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture ( JEPA ) models, developed by LeCunn and colleagues back in 2023, have been proposed for robots because they can take an action as input and ask what the world would be like with that action. But a JEPA world model produces an average of outcomes and would not be able to anticipate counterfactual scenarios – events that didn't happen. The technique that the researchers developed is not specific to JEPAs – it can be applied to any world model that predicts the average next state under any action. But JEPA models are particularly well suited to being adapted. Balestriero said that the counterfactual world model experiments were done using off-the-shelf encoders (DINOv2 and MAE) without any fine-tuning and only a small predictor trained on top. Creating a counterfactual world model from that starting point would only require minor additions. Counterfactual world models predict alternative scenarios more effectively by inferring possibilities from what did occur. "In causal inference, answering 'What would have happened had I acted differently?' takes three steps," explained Balestriero. "You use what you observed to learn something about those hidden factors, you change the action, and you predict again with the hidden factors kept exactly as they were. "Our counterfactual world model does all three steps with one subtraction." Balestriero cited an example from the paper: a boat crossing a river with a hidden current and how the JEPA world model and counterfactual world model predicted the boat's movements. "The world model predicted where the boat would end up after steering left, and it actually ended up two meters further downstream," he explained.

item.title: Netflix announces 'Stranger Things' spin-off 'Other Worlds', and it's already teasing a trip to Area 51 (video)
item.description: null So, you thought "Stranger Things" was done and dusted after all that Conformity Gate nonsense? No way! Netflix's sci-fi sensation returns in the live-action prequel series "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure." Created by the Duffer Brothers and Kate Trefry, with the episodes set to be directed by Joe Wright ("Darkest Hour", "Black Mirror"), this new show isn't set in Hawkins or the electric '80s. No, this time around, the action takes place in Marion, Nevada, in 1955, and you know what else is located in Nevada, right? Area 51 . The teaser trailer certainly teases the possibility of a trip to the world's most paradoxically famous secret military base, showcasing a bike and radio resting outside of a fence with a sign that clearly says it's a restricted area (in any TV show or film, that's actually an invitation to see what's on the other side). Of course, the tease doesn't end there, as the thunder booms in the sky and there's a visual hint of a wormhole. No story details about "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure" have been released to date, but there are some clues out there for all the Internet sleuths. Trefrey wrote the Henry Creel-focused "Stranger Things: The First Shadow" play, while Matt Duffer explained to Variety how a spin-off show would tackle the rock that Henry found in the briefcase in "Stranger Things." So, yes, expect this to be a Henry-centric affair and the start of his long, hard road to hell and becoming Vecna. (Image credit: Netflix) What'll be interesting, though, is to see how the show ties into the history of Area 51. After all, it was on April 12, 1955, that CIA officer Richard Bissell discovered the site, while the "Other Worlds" trailer has the date of April 19th clearly marked onscreen, so the timelines align nicely here. "Stranger Things" has never been shy of tying itself to real-world science and historical events, so it'll be fascinating to see how the show explores Area 51 as a concept and the secrets everybody believes are hidden there. Was it really a site to test highly advanced weapons and aircraft, or was E.T. 's cousin held hostage there until he revealed Colonel Sanders' 11 herbs and spices? Who knows, with all this renewed excitement around this mysterious military facility, we might get another "Storm Area 51" event to enjoy and laugh at all over again. Regardless, more "Stranger Things" is welcome news, and since it's presumably about one of the show's best characters, Henry Creel, it only adds another layer to his already intriguing lore. If we can't have an origin story about Hopper's incredible and envious moustache, this is the next best thing. "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure" arrives on Netflix in 2028. item.title: Social unrest ahead of French elections: Protesters 'don't believe politics can achieve anything'
item.description: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Renaud Foucart, Senior Lecturer at the Department of Economics ECARES at Lancaster University. France's 1.6% minimum-wage increase, in response to the countrywide protests, may offer a temporary reprieve from social unrest, but it does little to resolve the deeper political and institutional crisis confronting the country. According to Foucart, the central problem extends beyond declining purchasing power, fiscal constraints and the limitations of a minority government. It concerns a growing loss of faith in politics itself. “They are in the street because they don't believe politics can achieve anything,” Foucart argues, suggesting that the persistence of mass demonstrations ahead of the presidential election reflects profound disillusionment with the political system's capacity to deliver meaningful change.

item.title: Microsoft takes three decades to make Sticky Keys less sticky
item.description: Windows testers are getting a new option in the Sticky Keys and Filter Keys dialogs – one to banish the pop-ups without needing to venture deep into Settings. It's only taken several decades for Microsoft to put the off switch where the interruption actually happens. The accessibility features themselves are useful, though triggering their activation prompts by accident is another matter. Once enabled, Sticky Keys let users press modifier keys (such as Control) one at a time instead of holding them down together. For example, rather than holding Control and pressing C to copy, a user can press and release Control, then press C. Filter Keys, meanwhile, ignores brief or repeated keystrokes and adjusts the keyboard's repeat behavior. However, the dialogs are of little use to people who don't need the features, and they can pop up at the most inconvenient moments. Tap Shift five times, and you'll see what we mean: Windows chimes and shows a dialog asking whether you'd like to turn on Sticky Keys. Dismiss it, hit Shift five times, and there it is again. Or hold down the right Shift key for eight seconds to be treated to the Filter Keys pop-up. You can stop this behavior elsewhere in the system, but it requires a trek through Windows settings. The change, introduced in the Experimental Windows Insider Build 26340.9882, adds an option to the Sticky Keys or Filter Keys dialogs to dismiss the prompts permanently. It's a small change, but one that should spare users an irritating interruption. Better late than never – even if "never ask me again" has taken roughly three decades to reach the dialog. Former Microsoft engineer Charles Opperman said he wrote the dialog in early 1995 "after @bradsilverberg kids kept activating StickeyKeys [sic] while playing Space Cadet pinball." Opperman added that a link to Settings was added in Windows 98 or what would become Windows 2000, and a checkbox was considered even then, but it wasn't deemed a priority. Users could turn off the prompt via settings. Now the option is front and center. The option is also rolling out in the Windows Insider Beta channel , although Microsoft has not announced a general release date. ®

item.description: The management of Babcock University, Ilishan-Remo, Ogun State, has confirmed that a student involved in an incident at one of the institution’s residential facilities is alive and currently receiving medical attention at the university’s teaching hospital. This was communicated in a statement signed by the Associate Vice President, Communication, Media and Branding of the institution, Johnson Akintayo, who dismissed media reports suggesting that the student, whose identity is not disclosed, had died. The university said the student was receiving medical treatment alongside his roommate, who also sustained injuries during the incident. A video that surfaced online on Monday showed a student attempting to jump through the window of one of the university’s hostels as his roommates struggled to prevent him from attempting suicide. Following the incident, some media reports claimed that the student had died. “Contrary to reports suggesting that the student may have died, we wish to assure the public that he is responding positively to treatment and is receiving the necessary medical care,” Akintayo said. “The incident was brought under control by the commendable and prompt intervention of the student’s roommates, whose timely action prevented what could have been a more tragic outcome. “The student with one of his rescuers, however, sustained injuries in the process and were immediately taken for medical attention.” He further stated that the student’s parents had been contacted and were on campus to be with their ward as he receives treatment. Babcock University is a private tertiary institution in South-West Nigeria. (Photo: babcock.edu.ng) According to the statement, the other student who sustained an injury while rescuing his roommate has been “treated and discharged.” The university also disclosed that it had commenced an investigation to establish the immediate and underlying circumstances surrounding the incident. “This process will help us understand what happened, identify any factors that may have contributed to the situation, and determine appropriate measures to prevent a recurrence.” “The university therefore urges members of the public and media organisations to refrain from circulating unverified information or attributing causes to the incident while investigations are ongoing,” the statement added. “Beyond providing medical attention, the university said it was committed to supporting the student’s full recovery and well-being, adding that it would ensure appropriate support and guidance were made available to facilitate his recovery process ” “Babcock University takes the safety, health and welfare of its students and employees seriously. item.description: Carex, one of Nigeria’s leading personal hygiene brands, has successfully concluded its nationwide Everybody Wins Promo with a transparent Grand Finale Live Draw , rewarding loyal consumers and reinforcing its commitment to delivering value beyond personal care products. The campaign, which ran from June 2026 to August 2026, attracted millions of consumers PAN Nigeria and rewarded winners with prizes worth over ₦400,000,000. The Grand Finale Live Draw, held in Lagos, brought together consumers, media representatives, trade partners, regulatory officials, and other key stakeholders to witness the selection of the campaign’s grand prize winner through a transparent and independently supervised process. The event marked the culmination of months of consumer participation and engagement, further strengthening the connection between the Carex brand and its consumers. Throughout the promotion, participants had multiple opportunities to win exciting rewards, including instant Recharge Cards, shopping Vouchers, and a brand-new Car. Over 90,000 consumers emerged as winners over the course of the campaign. The grand prize car winner, Faith Stephen from Ijebu Ode, Ogun State, emerged through the live draw process conducted in accordance with all applicable promotional and regulatory requirements. Speaking at the event, Ifunanya Anwunah , Head of Category – Personal Hygiene, said: “At Carex, we believe that the consumers who trust our products every day deserve to be appreciated and rewarded. The Everybody Wins Promo was created as a tangible expression of our gratitude for the loyalty and support we continue to receive from Nigerian families. “ The overwhelming participation and enthusiasm witnessed throughout this campaign demonstrate the strong connection consumers have with the Carex brand. The promo was built on a simple promise: giving everyday consumers the opportunity to win meaningful rewards while enjoying the quality, care, and protection they have come to trust from Carex. As a brand trusted by millions of Nigerians for their personal hygiene and care needs, Carex remains committed to developing initiatives that deepen consumer engagement, reward loyalty, and create memorable experiences for consumers across the country. The successful completion of the Everybody Wins Promo further underscores the brand’s commitment to putting consumers at the heart of everything it does. About Carex Carex is committed to winning the war against germs through a range of antibacterial products that support the health, hygiene, and wellbeing of consumers. Through innovative products and engaging consumer initiatives, Carex continues to build meaningful connections with families across Nigeria, delivering trusted products that help consumers live healthier and more confident lives. item.title: BlackRock: Security Fears Are Driving Bitcoin Whales Into IBIT
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine BlackRock: Security Fears Are Driving Bitcoin Whales Into IBIT Large bitcoin holders are swapping coins they guard themselves for shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) at a record pace, the firm’s head of digital assets said Monday, as kidnappings and hacks push security to the top of their list. “The current moment is the highest we’ve seen at any point,” Robbie Mitchnick told Barron’s , adding that demand for the swaps “has sort of been one way — up.” Of all the reasons clients give, he said, “the single largest one is security and peace of mind.” The trades are in-kind conversions. A holder delivers bitcoin to the fund through an intermediary and receives newly created IBIT shares, without first selling the coins for cash. BlackRock relies on Galaxy Digital, Talos and Virtu to handle the transactions, and those firms set the minimum size. Barron’s put the volume BlackRock has seen at $3.6 billion, noting the real figure could be larger because the firm does not process every conversion itself. Mitchnick cited a bigger number in August, telling Bloomberg that IBIT had facilitated more than $5 billion of such swaps, up from more than $3 billion in October 2025 . In that August interview, BlackRock’s Mitchnick named the threats outright: “People see things happen in the outside world — whether it’s kidnappings, ransom, custody failures — that motivate them to make this switch for all or some of their holdings.” He told Barron’s the recent Binance hack was not news to big holders. “Most large Bitcoin holders were already acutely aware of the risk of holding on an exchange and in a hot wallet,” he said. How BlackRock’s swaps became possible The SEC voted on July 29, 2025, to let spot bitcoin and ether funds create and redeem shares in kind, ending the cash-only structure it required when the funds launched in January 2024. Access has widened since. BlackRock’s minimum started around $30 million and now hovers between $1 million and $2 million, Barron’s reported. Taxes are part of the pitch. Converting appreciated bitcoin into IBIT in kind “generally isn’t seen as a sale that would trigger capital-gains taxes,” Barron’s wrote, while Bloomberg cautioned that avoiding an immediate bill depends on the investor’s circumstances. Mitchnick also pointed to estate planning, calling it “much, much simpler” to hold the exposure “within the confines of their private bank.” Once inside, the coins sit with IBIT’s custodian, an affiliate of Coinbase Prime, in what Mitchnick called an “institutional-grade cold-storage model.” The fund held 795,921 BTC, worth about $60.4 billion, as of Nov. 6. Why the flow numbers overstate demand An in-kind creation adds IBIT shares and counts toward the fund’s reported flows, but no bitcoin is bought on the open market. The coins already existed and simply changed wrappers, so headline flow figures overstate new cash. Cash has been moving the other way. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $1.28 billion
